description: Three girls, one Professor, and a universe of possibilities.
summary:
Kozmik Bostan is a browser-based pixel-art game that turns lunar exploration and space agriculture into a personal journey. Stranded on the Moon, the player must grow food, manage limited oxygen, water and energy, and repair a spacecraft to return to Earth.

Across eight connected missions, players explore the lunar surface, collect supplies and care for crops through interactive planting, watering and harvesting activities. Science and history cards connect discoveries in the game to space exploration, including Apollo artifacts and lunar laser ranging.

The project helps students and curious players understand how survival systems depend on one another. Every trip and every crop requires choices about limited resources. With Turkish and English interfaces and controls for computers and phones, Kozmik Bostan makes these ideas accessible through play. The journey ends with the astronaut bringing home a zinnia grown on the Moon, giving the scientific experience an emotional conclusion.
details:
Kozmik Bostan is a 2D exploration and resource-management game set on the Moon. The player follows a stranded astronaut through eight missions, growing food and repairing a spacecraft to return home.

The gameplay connects exploration with the practical demands of survival. Leaving the base consumes oxygen, while the greenhouse needs water and power to keep crops growing. Players collect supplies, repair equipment and decide when to return to safety. Interactive greenhouse activities let them plant seeds, cover them with soil, water crops and harvest the results. These actions make the relationship between resources and survival visible through their consequences.

Exploration also creates opportunities to learn. Science and history cards introduce topics such as Apollo artifacts and lunar laser ranging. Players encounter these explanations at relevant locations, connecting what they discover to the activity they are performing.

We developed the game using TypeScript, Phaser and Vite, with browser-based interfaces and local progress saving. The project is hosted on Vercel. It supports Turkish and English, keyboard and touch controls, and separate normal and quick-play modes. Accessibility considerations include reduced motion and adjustable touch controls.

Our intended audience includes school students, science center visitors and players interested in space exploration. The game could support classroom discussions about resource use or provide a short interactive experience at science events. Its intended impact is to encourage curiosity and help players reason about connected systems. Learning outcomes have yet to be measured through a structured user study.

The story gives players a personal reason to complete the mission. After repairing the spacecraft, the astronaut returns to Earth carrying a zinnia grown on the Moon for someone they love.
